sanskrit: sa hi brahmavidāṃ śreṣṭho brahmāstre cāpy anuttamaḥ tasmād droṇaḥ parājaiṣīn māṃ vai sa sakhivigrahe
english: For he is the foremost among those who know the Brahman, and peerless in the Brahma-weapon as well; it was for this reason that Droṇa defeated me in that conflict with my friend.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo nāsti tulyo 'sya pṛthivyāṃ kaś cid agraṇīḥ kauravācāryamukhyasya bhāradvājasya dhīmataḥ
english: There is no warrior anywhere on earth who is his equal, no one who stands foremost — that wise Bhāradvāja, the chief preceptor of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: droṇasya śarajālāni prāṇidehaharāṇi ca ṣaḍaratni dhanuś cāsya dṛśyate 'pratimaṃ mahat
english: Droṇa's volleys of arrows strip away both life and body, and his bow — six cubits long — appears vast and without equal.

sanskrit: sa hi brāhmaṇavegena kṣātraṃ vegam asaṃśayam pratihanti maheṣvāso bhāradvājo mahāmanāḥ
english: That great-souled great archer Bhāradvāja, with the force of a Brahmin, checks without doubt the force of the warrior class.

sanskrit: kṣatrocchedāya vihito jāmadagnya ivāsthitaḥ tasya hy astrabalaṃ ghoram aprasahyaṃ narair bhuvi
english: Stationed like Jāmadagnya, he is ordained for the destruction of the Kṣatriyas; his terrible power of arms is indeed irresistible by men on earth.

sanskrit: brāhmam uccārayaṃs tejo hutāhutir ivānalaḥ sametya sa dahaty ājau kṣatraṃ brahmapuraḥsaraḥ brahmakṣatre ca vihite brahmatejo viśiṣyate
english: Pouring forth Brahmic energy like a fire fed with oblations, he consumes the warrior class in battle with the Brahman going before him; and when Brahmin and Kṣatriya power are ranged against each other, Brahmic energy prevails.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ kṣatrabalād dhīno brahmatejaḥ prapedivān droṇād viśiṣṭam āsādya bhavantaṃ brahmavittamam
english: I, fallen short in the power of the warrior class and seeking Brahmic energy, have come to you — superior even to Droṇa and the most learned of those who know the Brahman.

sanskrit: droṇāntakam ahaṃ putraṃ labheyaṃ yudhi durjayam tat karma kuru me yāja nirvapāmy arbudaṃ gavām
english: I wish to obtain a son who will be Droṇa's death-in-battle, unconquerable in war — perform this rite for me, O Yāja; I will give you a hundred million cows.

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tu taṃ yājo yājyārtham upakalpayat gurvartha iti cākāmam upayājam acodayat yājo droṇavināśāya pratijajñe tathā ca saḥ
english: Yāja agreed, saying 'so be it,' and prepared for the sacrifice on behalf of the patron; for the teacher's sake he also urged Upayāja, who was unwilling; and Yāja thus pledged himself for Droṇa's destruction.

sanskrit: tatas tasya narendrasya upayājo mahātapāḥ ācakhyau karma vaitānaṃ tadā putraphalāya vai
english: Then the great ascetic Upayāja explained to that lord of men the sacrificial rite that would yield a son as its fruit.

sanskrit: sa ca putro mahāvīryo mahātejā mahābalaḥ iṣyate yadvidho rājan bhavitā te tathāvidhaḥ
english: "The son you desire — O king, one of great heroism, great energy and great strength — shall be just such a one as you wish."

sanskrit: bhāradvājasya hantāraṃ so 'bhisaṃdhāya bhūmipaḥ ājahre tat tathā sarvaṃ drupadaḥ karmasiddhaye
english: With the intention of obtaining the slayer of Bhāradvāja's son, king Drupada had all of that duly carried out for the success of the rite.

sanskrit: yājas tu havanasyānte devīm āhvāpayat tadā praihi māṃ rājñi pṛṣati mithunaṃ tvām upasthitam
english: Then at the end of the oblation Yāja called out to the queen: "Come to me, O queen Pṛṣatī — a pair is ready awaiting you."

sanskrit: devy uvāca avaliptaṃ me mukhaṃ brahman puṇyān gandhān bibharmi ca sutārthenoparuddhāsmi tiṣṭha yāja mama priye
english: The queen said: "My face is anointed, O Brahmin, and I bear sacred fragrances upon me; I am detained on account of my desire for a son — wait for me, O Yāja, my dear."

sanskrit: yāja uvāca yājena śrapitaṃ havyam upayājena mantritam kathaṃ kāmaṃ na saṃdadhyāt sā tvaṃ vipraihi tiṣṭha vā
english: Yāja said: "The oblation has been cooked by Yāja and consecrated by Upayāja — how can it fail to fulfil your wish? Come, O Brahmin lady, or stay as you will."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca evam ukte tu yājena hute haviṣi saṃskṛte uttasthau pāvakāt tasmāt kumāro devasaṃnibhaḥ
english: The narrator said: When Yāja had spoken thus, and the oblation had been poured and duly sanctified, a boy resembling a god arose from that fire.

sanskrit: jvālāvarṇo ghorarūpaḥ kirīṭī varma cottamam bibhrat sakhaḍgaḥ saśaro dhanuṣmān vinadan muhuḥ
english: Flame-colored, of terrible aspect, wearing a diadem and bearing the finest armor, sword in hand, arrow-equipped, bow in hand, he roared again and again.

sanskrit: so 'dhyārohad rathavaraṃ tena ca prayayau tadā tataḥ praṇeduḥ pāñcālāḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ sādhu sādhv iti
english: He mounted a splendid chariot and set out in it; then the Pāñcālas shouted in delight, "Excellent! Excellent!"

sanskrit: bhayāpaho rājaputraḥ pāñcālānāṃ yaśaskaraḥ rājñaḥ śokāpaho jāta eṣa droṇavadhāya vai ity uvāca mahad bhūtam adṛśyaṃ khecaraṃ tadā
english: "This prince, dispeller of fear, bringer of glory to the Pāñcālas, dispeller of the king's grief — he is born truly for the slaying of Droṇa!" — so said a great invisible being that moved through the sky at that time.

sanskrit: kumārī cāpi pāñcālī vedimadhyāt samutthitā subhagā darśanīyāṅgī vedimadhyā manoramā
english: A maiden of Pāñcāla also arose from the midst of the sacrificial altar — lovely, beautiful of limb, slender-waisted, and delightful.

sanskrit: śyāmā padmapalāśākṣī nīlakuñcitamūrdhajā mānuṣaṃ vigrahaṃ kṛtvā sākṣād amaravarṇinī
english: Dark-complexioned, with eyes like lotus petals, curling dark hair, she bore a human form yet was visibly of celestial beauty.

sanskrit: nīlotpalasamo gandho yasyāḥ krośāt pravāyati yā bibharti paraṃ rūpaṃ yasyā nāsty upamā bhuvi
english: From her wafted the fragrance of a blue lotus, perceptible from a league away; she bore supreme beauty for which there was no comparison on earth.

sanskrit: tāṃ cāpi jātāṃ suśroṇīṃ vāg uvācāśarīriṇī sarvayoṣidvarā kṛṣṇā kṣayaṃ kṣatraṃ ninīṣati
english: And as she of lovely hips was born, a bodiless voice spoke: "This Kṛṣṇā, foremost of all women, will bring about the destruction of the Kṣatriyas."

sanskrit: surakāryam iyaṃ kāle kariṣyati sumadhyamā asyā hetoḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahad utpatsyate bhayam
english: "This slender-waisted one will in time accomplish the work of the gods; on her account a great terror will arise among the Kṣatriyas."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā sarvapāñcālāḥ praṇeduḥ siṃhasaṃghavat na caitān harṣasaṃpūṇān iyaṃ sehe vasuṃdharā
english: Hearing this, all the Pāñcālas roared like a pride of lions; the earth could not bear those who were filled with such joy.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā pṛṣatī yājaṃ prapede vai sutārthinī na vai mad anyāṃ jananīṃ jānīyātām imāv iti
english: Seeing the two, Pṛṣatī — who had desired children — approached Yāja, saying: "Let these two know no other mother than me."

sanskrit: tathety uvāca tāṃ yājo rājñaḥ priyacikīrṣayā tayoś ca nāmanī cakrur dvijāḥ saṃpūrṇamānasāḥ
english: Yāja said "so be it" to her, wishing to please the king; and the twice-born, their hearts full of joy, gave names to the two.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭatvād atidhṛṣṭutvād dharmād dyutsaṃbhavād api dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ kumāro 'yaṃ drupadasya bhavatv iti
english: "Because of his boldness and exceeding audacity, and because he arose from the sacred fire's brilliance, let this boy of Drupada be called Dhṛṣṭadyumna."

sanskrit: kṛṣṇety evābruvan kṛṣṇāṃ kṛṣṇābhūt sā hi varṇataḥ tathā tan mithunaṃ jajñe drupadasya mahāmakhe
english: They called the girl Kṛṣṇā, for she was dark of complexion. Thus that twin pair was born at Drupada's great sacrifice.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tu pāñcālyam ānīya svaṃ viveśanam upākarod astrahetor bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān
english: Taking Dhṛṣṭadyumna of Pāñcāla into his own residence, the powerful Bhāradvāja trained him in the use of weapons.

sanskrit: amokṣaṇīyaṃ daivaṃ hi bhāvi matvā mahāmatiḥ tathā tat kṛtavān droṇa ātmakīrty anurakṣaṇāt
english: The great-minded Droṇa, understanding that what is destined cannot be escaped, did this nonetheless — to preserve his own glory.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā tu kaunteyāḥ śalyaviddhā ivābhavan sarve cāsvasthamanaso babhūvus te mahārathāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, the sons of Kuntī became as if pierced by lances, and those great warriors were all unsettled in mind.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuntī sutān dṛṣṭvā vibhrāntān gatacetasaḥ yudhiṣṭhiram uvācedaṃ vacanaṃ satyavādinī
english: Then Kuntī, seeing her sons distraught and out of their senses, spoke these words to Yudhiṣṭhira — she who ever speaks the truth.

sanskrit: cirarātroṣitāḥ smeha brāhmaṇasya niveśane ramamāṇāḥ pure ramye labdhabhaikṣā yudhiṣṭhira
english: "We have lodged here for a long time in the dwelling of the Brahmin, taking our pleasure in this delightful city and obtaining our alms, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yānīha ramaṇīyāni vanāny upavanāni ca sarvāṇi tāni dṛṣṭāni punaḥ punar ariṃdama
english: All the lovely forests and groves here have been seen again and again, O subduer of enemies.

sanskrit: punar dṛṣṭāni tāny eva prīṇayanti na nas tathā bhaikṣaṃ ca na tathā vīra labhyate kurunandana
english: Seen again and again, they no longer delight us as before; and alms too are not obtained as they were, O hero, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ sādhu pāñcālān gacchāma yadi manyase apūrvadarśanaṃ tāta ramaṇīyaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Let us go to Pāñcāla — if you think it good; we shall see things never seen before, my son, and it will be delightful.

sanskrit: subhikṣāś caiva pāñcālāḥ śrūyante śatrukarśana yajñasenaś ca rājāsau brahmaṇya iti śuśrumaḥ
english: The Pāñcālas are said to be prosperous, O you who wear down enemies, and that king Yajñasena too we have heard is devoted to Brahmins.

sanskrit: ekatra ciravāso hi kṣamo na ca mato mama te tatra sādhu gacchāmo yadi tvaṃ putra manyase
english: Long dwelling in one place is not good, and is not my view; let us go there to Pāñcāla — if you think so, my son."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhavatyā yan mataṃ kāryaṃ tad asmākaṃ paraṃ hitam anujāṃs tu na jānāmi gaccheyur neti vā punaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Whatever you consider should be done is our highest good; as for my younger brothers, I know not whether they will go or not."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kuntī bhīmasenam arjunaṃ yamajau tathā uvāca gamanaṃ te ca tathety evābruvaṃs tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Kuntī spoke of the journey to Bhīmasena, Arjuna, and the twins, and they too said "so be it" at that time.

sanskrit: tata āmantrya taṃ vipraṃ kuntī rājan sutaiḥ saha pratasthe nagarīṃ ramyāṃ drupadasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then, O king, Kuntī took leave of that Brahmin and set out together with her sons for the lovely city of the great-souled Drupada.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vasatsu teṣu pracchannaṃ pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu ājagāmātha tān draṣṭuṃ vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While those great-souled Pāṇḍavas were dwelling in disguise, Vyāsa the son of Satyavatī came to see them.

sanskrit: tam āgatam abhiprekṣya pratyudgamya paraṃtapāḥ praṇipatyābhivādyainaṃ tasthuḥ prāñjalayas tadā
english: Seeing him arrive, those scorchers of enemies went forward to meet him, bowed down to him and greeted him, and then stood with hands joined in reverence.

sanskrit: samanujñāpya tān sarvān āsīnān munir abravīt prasannaḥ pūjitaḥ pārthaiḥ prītipūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having given them all leave to be seated, the sage, pleased and honored by the sons of Pṛthā, spoke these words with affection.

sanskrit: api dharmeṇa vartadhvaṃ śāstreṇa ca paraṃtapāḥ api vipreṣu vaḥ pūjā pūjārheṣu na hīyate
english: "Are you conducting yourselves according to dharma and the scriptures, O scorchers of enemies? Is your reverence toward the Brahmins who deserve reverence not diminishing?"

sanskrit: atha dharmārthavad vākyam uktvā sa bhagavān ṛṣiḥ vicitrāś ca kathās tās tāḥ punar evedam abravīt
english: Having spoken words full of righteousness and purpose, and various other stories, that blessed sage then spoke again as follows.

sanskrit: āsīt tapovane kā cid ṛṣeḥ kanyā mahātmanaḥ vilagnamadhyā suśroṇī subhrūḥ sarvaguṇānvitā
english: "In a forest of asceticism there was once the daughter of a great-souled sage — slender-waisted, lovely-hipped, with beautiful brows, endowed with every virtue.

sanskrit: karmabhiḥ svakṛtaiḥ sā tu durbhagā samapadyata nādhyagacchat patiṃ sā tu kanyā rūpavatī satī
english: Yet through deeds done by herself she became ill-fated; that virtuous and beautiful maiden found no husband.

sanskrit: tapas taptum athārebhe patyartham asukhā tataḥ toṣayām āsa tapasā sā kilogreṇa śaṃkaram
english: Unhappy, she then undertook to practice austerities for the sake of a husband, and with severe asceticism she propitiated Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ sa bhagavāṃs tuṣṭas tām uvāca tapasvinīm varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te varado 'smīti bhāmini
english: The blessed god, pleased with her, spoke to that ascetic woman: 'Choose a boon, fair one — good fortune to you; I am the giver of boons.'

sanskrit: atheśvaram uvācedam ātmanaḥ sā vaco hitam patiṃ sarvaguṇopetam icchāmīti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then she spoke to the Lord what was beneficial for her: 'I desire a husband endowed with every virtue' — she said this again and again.

sanskrit: tām atha pratyuvācedam īśāno vadatāṃ varaḥ pañca te patayo bhadre bhaviṣyantīti śaṃkaraḥ
english: Then the Lord, the best of speakers, replied to her: 'Five husbands shall be yours, O auspicious one' — so said Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: pratibruvantīm ekaṃ me patiṃ dehīti śaṃkaram punar evābravīd deva idaṃ vacanam uttamam
english: As she replied 'Give me one husband, O Śaṃkara,' he said to her once again these excellent words, O god:

sanskrit: pañcakṛtvas tvayā uktaḥ patiṃ dehīty ahaṃ punaḥ deham anyaṃ gatāyās te yathoktaṃ tad bhaviṣyati
english: 'You have said to me five times \"give me a husband\"; when you have passed into another body, what I have said shall come to pass.'

sanskrit: drupadasya kule jātā kanyā sā devarūpiṇī nirdiṣṭā bhavatāṃ patnī kṛṣṇā pārṣaty aninditā
english: 'That maiden of divine appearance, born in Drupada's family — the blameless Kṛṣṇā Pārṣatī — is appointed as your wife.'

sanskrit: pāñcālanagaraṃ tasmāt praviśadhvaṃ mahābalāḥ sukhinas tām anuprāpya bhaviṣyatha na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'Therefore enter the city of Pāñcāla, O men of great might; having obtained her you will be happy — there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābhāgaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ pitāmahaḥ pārthān āmantrya kuntīṃ ca prātiṣṭhata mahātapāḥ
english: Having spoken thus, that most blessed grandfather of the Pāṇḍavas, the great ascetic, took leave of the sons of Pṛthā and Kuntī and departed.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te pratasthuḥ puraskṛtya mātaraṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ samair udaṅmukhair mārgair yathoddiṣṭaṃ paraṃtapāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those bulls among men, scorchers of enemies, set out with their mother placed in front, following level northward roads as directed.

sanskrit: te gacchantas tv ahorātraṃ tīrthaṃ somaśravāyaṇam āseduḥ puruṣavyāghrā gaṅgāyāṃ pāṇḍunandanāḥ
english: Traveling for a day and a night, those tigers among men, the sons of Pāṇḍu, reached the Somaśravāyaṇa ford on the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: ulmukaṃ tu samudyamya teṣām agre dhanaṃjayaḥ prakāśārthaṃ yayau tatra rakṣārthaṃ ca mahāyaśāḥ
english: Lifting up a firebrand, the greatly famous Dhanaṃjaya went in front of them — to give light and for protection.

sanskrit: tatra gaṅgājale ramye vivikte krīḍayan striyaḥ īrṣyur gandharvarājaḥ sma jalakrīḍām upāgataḥ
english: There, in the lovely waters of the Gaṅgā in a secluded spot, the jealous king of Gandharvas had come for water-sports, sporting with women.

sanskrit: śabdaṃ teṣāṃ sa śuśrāva nadīṃ samupasarpatām tena śabdena cāviṣṭaś cukrodha balavad balī
english: He heard the sound of them approaching the river; possessed by that sound, that powerful one became extremely angry.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavāṃs tatra saha mātrā paraṃtapān visphārayan dhanur ghoram idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing the Pāṇḍavas there together with their mother, those scorchers of enemies, he twanged his terrible bow and spoke these words.

sanskrit: saṃdhyā saṃrajyate ghorā pūrvarātrāgameṣu yā aśītibhis truṭair hīnaṃ taṃ muhūrtaṃ pracakṣate
english: "The terrible twilight that glows red at the coming of the early night — that moment, they say, is lacking eighty truṭas of the full period.

sanskrit: vihitaṃ kāmacārāṇāṃ yakṣagandharvarakṣasām śeṣam anyan manuṣyāṇāṃ kāmacāram iha smṛtam
english: That time is ordained for the free movement of Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas; what remains besides is remembered here as the time for men to move at will.

sanskrit: lobhāt pracāraṃ caratas tāsu velāsu vai narān upakrāntā nigṛhṇīmo rākṣasaiḥ saha bāliśān
english: Those foolish men who out of greed roam about at those hours — together with the Rākṣasas we seize and restrain those who transgress.

sanskrit: tato rātrau prāpnuvato jalaṃ brahmavido janāḥ garhayanti narān sarvān balasthān nṛpatīn api
english: Those who know the Brahman censure all men who approach the water at night — even the powerful, even kings.

sanskrit: ārāt tiṣṭhata mā mahyaṃ samīpam upasarpata kasmān māṃ nābhijānīta prāptaṃ bhāgīrathījalam
english: Stand far off — do not approach near to me! Why do you not recognize me who has come to the waters of the Bhāgīrathī?

sanskrit: aṅgāraparṇaṃ gandharvaṃ vitta māṃ svabalāśrayam ahaṃ hi mānī cerṣyuś ca kuberasya priyaḥ sakhā
english: Know me to be the Gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa, one who relies on his own strength; I am proud and jealous, and the beloved friend of Kubera.

sanskrit: aṅgāraparṇam iti ca khyataṃ vanam idaṃ mama anu gaṅgāṃ ca vākāṃ ca citraṃ yatra vasāmy aham
english: This forest of mine is known as Aṅgāraparṇa — the beautiful one along the Gaṅgā and the Vākā — where I dwell.

sanskrit: na kuṇapāḥ śṛṅgiṇo vā na devā na ca mānuṣāḥ idaṃ samupasarpanti tat kiṃ samupasarpatha
english: Neither ghosts nor horned beasts, neither gods nor human beings approach this place — why then do you approach it?"

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca samudre himavatpārśve nadyām asyāṃ ca durmate rātrāv ahani saṃdhau ca kasya kḷptaḥ parigrahaḥ
english: Arjuna said: "On the ocean, on the slopes of Himavat, or on this river, O wicked-minded one — whose domain is established for the night, the day, or the twilight?

sanskrit: vayaṃ ca śaktisaṃpannā akāle tvām adhṛṣṇumaḥ aśaktā hi kṣaṇe krūre yuṣmān arcanti mānavāḥ
english: We are endowed with power and do not fear you even at an improper time; it is those who are powerless that honor you in a moment of danger.

sanskrit: purā himavataś caiṣā hemaśṛṅgād viniḥsṛtā gaṅgā gatvā samudrāmbhaḥ saptadhā pratipadyate
english: "Of old this Gaṅgā issued forth from Himavat's golden peak, and flowing to the ocean's waters divides itself into seven streams.

sanskrit: iyaṃ bhūtvā caikavaprā śucir ākāśagā punaḥ deveṣu gaṅgā gandharva prāpnoty alakanandatām
english: And again, flowing pure as one stream through the sky, this Gaṅgā attains among the gods, O Gandharva, the form of the Alakanandā.

sanskrit: tathā pitṝn vaitaraṇī dustarā pāpakarmabhiḥ gaṅgā bhavati gandharva yathā dvaipāyano 'bravīt
english: In the same way, for the ancestors she becomes the Vaitaraṇī, impassable by those of wicked deeds, O Gandharva — as Dvaipāyana has declared.

sanskrit: asaṃbādhā devanadī svargasaṃpādanī śubhā katham icchasi tāṃ roddhuṃ naiṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: This unobstructed, auspicious divine river that leads to heaven — how do you wish to block it? This is not eternal dharma.

sanskrit: anivāryam asaṃbādhaṃ tava vācā kathaṃ vayam na spṛśema yathākāmaṃ puṇyaṃ bhāgīrathījalam
english: How should we not touch at will the sacred waters of the Bhāgīrathī, which cannot be stopped and is unobstructed — how can your words prevent us?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca aṅgāraparṇas tac chrutvā kruddha ānamya kārmukam mumoca sāyakān dīptān ahīn āśīviṣān iva
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that, Aṅgāraparṇa in fury bent his bow and discharged blazing arrows like venomous serpents.
